solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soft skin binding books

indicators.note: the skin word wraps round the books, as a binding holds pages

parts.note: to flay is to skin
B is book; doubled, BB stands for books

explanation.surface: A bookbinder covering volumes in soft leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby flesh is limp and lacking firmness, which is to say soft.

clue.text: Female crew put in fashion goods for transport

indicators.note: the rowing crew is placed inside the fashion word

parts.note: a rage is a craze, a fashion
an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A women's rowing team modelling clothes for transit.
explanation.definitionFit: Freightage is cargo, the load of goods carried by a ship or vehicle.

clue.text: Troubling care reports not opened by bishop on time

indicators.note: the reports word loses its opening letter, the bishop's

parts.note: bangs are loud reports
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A worried bishop ignoring alarming news about the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is deep anxiety or dread, a troubling worry.

clue.text: Portable heater in warm country briefly turned on

indicators.note: the country loses its last letter

parts.note: Brazil is a hot country

indicators.note: turned sends the regarding word the other way

parts.note: re means on, about

explanation.surface: Switching on a heater while staying somewhere hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned on' looks like switching on; it is RE (on, concerning) read backwards as ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazier is a metal basket of burning coals that can be carried, used for outdoor warmth.

clue.text: Old boy, like boor in back street, pushes in

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: the boorish word sits inside the street abbreviation
back has the street abbreviation read in reverse order

parts.note: a boor is rude

explanation.surface: An uncouth former pupil barging his way into a back street.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to thrust oneself forward uninvited, intruding where not wanted.

clue.text: Artist taken in by Garbo's charms

indicators.note: the name lies inside the phrase, swallowed by its letters

explanation.surface: A painter falling for the allure of actress Greta Garbo.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was the Dutch painter of The Garden of Earthly Delights.

clue.text: Engineers on circuit secure drained sink again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
a lap is a circuit

indicators.note: secure emptied of its inner letters leaves only its ends

explanation.surface: Engineers repairing a waste circuit to fix a blocked sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' is the verb, to decline, not the kitchen basin.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into a worse state, sinking once more.

clue.text: Dog chewed up dad's unopened lunch, swallowing hard

indicators.note: the mangled mixture takes the hard letter inside
chewed up has these letters mashed into a new order
lunch without its first letter

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A pet wolfing down its owner's packed meal.
explanation.walkthrough: DADS with UNCH rearranges to DACHSUND, which swallows H.
explanation.definitionFit: The dachshund is a long-bodied, short-legged German breed of hound.

clue.text: Fabulous river bears you might catch

indicators.note: catching a word means hearing it spoken

parts.note: sticks means puts up with, bears

explanation.surface: Wild bears that could be caught along a legendary river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Styx is the river of the Greek underworld in myth.

clue.text: Chinese art best unframed if hung freely

indicators.note: freely lets the letters move loose into a fresh order
best without its outer letters, the frame

explanation.surface: Advice that a painting looks best hung without a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Feng shui is the Chinese practice of arranging surroundings for harmony.

clue.text: Craftsmen increasingly important in small spaces

indicators.note: the weightier word is placed within the printers' spaces

parts.note: an en is a small printing space; ENS is the plural
graver means more serious, more important

explanation.surface: Artisans gaining status while working in cramped workshops.
explanation.walkthrough: In typesetting an en is a space half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: Engravers are skilled workers who cut designs into metal, wood or stone.

clue.text: Chance intrepid leader's missing

indicators.note: the first letter of the brave word is dropped

parts.note: intrepid means plucky

explanation.surface: A daring commander is absent, leaving things to chance.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, a chance discovery is a fortunate, accidental one, i.e. lucky.

clue.text: Gaining ground she put husband in losing position

parts.note: gaining means getting

indicators.note: ground, as in milled, has these letters pulverised and reformed

explanation.surface: A wife makes headway in a domestic power struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is the past tense of grind, not land; the husband's letter is put in at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the push is an idiom for being dismissed from a job, i.e. losing it.

clue.text: Variant non-U creeds not officially restricted

indicators.note: a variant is a different form, so the letters take another order

explanation.surface: Unconventional religious beliefs being openly tolerated.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is the old label for language thought not upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncensored material has not been cut or suppressed by any authority.

clue.text: Person hauling loom

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who tows (rhymes with 'mower')
second meaning: to loom over something (rhymes with 'power')

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: a towing person versus to rise high.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower drags vehicles along, and to tower above is to loom large overhead.

clue.text: More prudent coastal state trapped wolf

indicators.note: the prudent word holds the state captive inside

parts.note: wiser means more prudent
Oman is a state on the Arabian coast

explanation.surface: A cautious nation catching a predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wolf' looks like the animal; it is slang for a predatory pursuer of women.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf is slang for a man who chases women, a philanderer.

clue.text: Comic character, one of five joining race around lake

indicators.note: the racing word surrounds the lake abbreviation

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, race
L is the map abbreviation for lake
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: One of a set of quintuplets enters a race around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is the stock clown figure of the commedia dell'arte and pantomime.

clue.text: Taciturn stoic regularly going in late

indicators.note: the picked letters enter the late word

parts.note: late means recent

indicators.note: every other letter of stoic

explanation.surface: A stoical person quietly arriving late.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticent person is reserved and says little, which is what taciturn describes.

clue.text: Willing tip to bring sporting advantage

parts.note: game means willing, up for it
a tip is a point, an end

explanation.surface: Advice about how an eager player gains an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a game point is the stage where one more won rally wins the game.

clue.text: Sunshade under pressure popping

indicators.note: in this down entry the sunshade sits below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
an awning is a canopy for shade

explanation.surface: A sun canopy bursting under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popping' is British slang for pawning, as in 'pop goes the weasel'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop something is informal British for pawning it at a pawnbroker's for cash.

clue.text: Beg last of Oxford dons to shut up

indicators.note: the final letter puts on the enclosing word like clothing, ending up inside it

parts.note: to cage is to shut up

indicators.note: takes the final letter of Oxford

explanation.surface: Academics at Oxford being told to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers but is the verb 'puts on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge is to scrounge or ask for something free, a form of begging.

clue.text: Striking means of locating milk supplier?

definitions.text: Striking means of locating milk supplier?

parts.words: Striking means of locating milk supplier?
parts.note: a bell, struck as the animal moves, hung round a dairy animal's neck so it can be found

explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' means hit, as a bell is, not impressive; the milk supplier is the animal, not a dairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowbell hangs from a cow's collar and rings so the herd can be traced.

clue.text: Has complete understanding, with hindsight?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to know something backwards is to know it thoroughly
second meaning, whimsical: knowing by looking back

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes thorough mastery of a subject, while literally it suggests knowledge gained in reverse.

clue.text: Sometimes streaky British painter?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cured pork, of which streaky is one cut
second meaning: Francis ..., the British artist

explanation.walkthrough: Streaky bacon is the fatty cut from the belly; the painter could seem a streaky one.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaky is a kind of bacon, and Francis Bacon was a celebrated twentieth-century British painter.

clue.text: Revived you with kiss after wine

indicators.note: after puts the you-and-kiss pair second, behind the wine

parts.note: red is a wine
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: Bringing someone round with a kiss after drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Redux, placed after a noun, means brought back or restored, as in a revived version.

clue.text: After Berliner's agreement, go to French island

parts.note: ja is German for yes
va is French for go

explanation.surface: A German agrees and heads off to an island off France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French island' looks like a single phrase; French belongs to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Java is the large Indonesian island where Jakarta stands.

clue.text: Scorer's very "detailed" attack

indicators.note: de-tailed: its tail, the final letter, is removed

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: A sports report on how thoroughly the attacking side played.
explanation.walkthrough: The scorer is a composer writing a score; in musical directions assai means very.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian musical term meaning very, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Hoodwink impressionable candidate

parts.note: to con is to hoodwink
tender means young and impressionable

explanation.surface: Deceiving a naive applicant in an election or job race.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is someone competing for a title or post, a candidate.

clue.text: Proud, contrary attempt to break rank

indicators.note: the reversed attempt splits the rank word open

parts.note: rank and arrant both mean utter, downright

indicators.note: contrary has the attempt word facing the other way

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A haughty, defiant soldier trying to break ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' here is the adjective meaning utter, not a row of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogant means haughty and self-important, an excessive sense of pride.

clue.text: Crooked old partner has absconded to the borders

indicators.note: the escaping word forms the borders, sitting either side of the former partner

parts.note: fled means ran off, absconded
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A dishonest former spouse has fled towards the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' suggests dishonest; here it is bent, as in a flexed arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexed limb is bent at the joint, which is to say crooked.
